title: Connections: Time Travel
desc: What links these historical facts? Spot the thread across centuries

questions.q: What connects: the fall of Constantinople (1453), Columbus reaching America (1492), and the printing press (~1440)?
questions.a: They all mark the transition from the Medieval period to the Renaissance / Age of Exploration — the end of one era and the birth of the modern world within a 50-year window

questions.q: What connects: penicillin, X-rays, and the microwave oven?
questions.a: All were discovered by accident — Fleming's mouldy petri dish, Röntgen's fluorescent screen, and Percy Spencer's melted chocolate bar near a magnetron

questions.q: Odd one out: Roman Empire, Ottoman Empire, British Empire, Mongol Empire. Which and why?
questions.a: Mongol Empire — it's the only one that was never a naval power. The others all had significant maritime reach

questions.q: What connects: Harriet Tubman, Oskar Schindler, and Raoul Wallenberg?
questions.a: All risked their lives to save persecuted people — Tubman (enslaved people via the Underground Railroad), Schindler (Jews during the Holocaust), Wallenberg (Jews in Budapest with protective passports)

questions.q: Put these inventions in chronological order: compass, gunpowder, printing press, telescope
questions.a: Compass (~1100) → gunpowder (~1200s in Europe, earlier in China) → printing press (~1440) → telescope (1608)

questions.q: What connects: Napoleon, Elba, and St Helena?
questions.a: Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814, escaped, returned to power for 100 days, was defeated at Waterloo, then exiled again to St Helena where he died

questions.q: Which three countries were on the losing side in BOTH World War I and World War II?
questions.a: Germany, Austria (Austria-Hungary in WWI), and — controversially — Turkey/Ottoman Empire in WWI, though Turkey was neutral in most of WWII. The clean answer is Germany and Austria; the third is often debated (Hungary, Bulgaria)

questions.q: What connects: the Suez Canal, the Panama Canal, and the Corinth Canal?
questions.a: All are artificial waterways cut through land to shorten sea routes — and all were engineering megaprojects that took decades, cost enormous human life, and reshaped global trade

questions.q: True, false, or it depends: 'Vikings wore horned helmets'
questions.a: False — no archaeological evidence supports horned helmets. The myth comes from 19th-century Romantic opera and art
Pivotal years of revolution/invasion — Norman Conquest of England (1066), American Declaration of Independence (1776), French Revolution (1789)
